newsitem.title: JAPAN: NORDIC SKIING-SKIERS UNDERGO PRE-RACE BLOOD TESTS.
newsitem.headline: NORDIC SKIING-SKIERS UNDERGO PRE-RACE BLOOD TESTS.

text.p: Cross-country skiers competing in a World Cup event on Saturday became the first athletes in an Olympic sport to undergo pre-race tests for illegal blood-doping.

Forty skiers -- 20 men and 20 women -- were selected randomly from some 90 entrants to provide blood samples, which were analysed for haemoglobin levels before the competition began. None failed the tests.

High haemoglobin levels boost endurance by enabling the blood to transport more oxygen to working muscles. Athletes can increase haemoglobin levels by training at altitude or even by sleeping in an artificially pressurised room.

Silvio Fauner of Italy, winner of the men's 10-km classic event, who was among those selected for testing, voiced support for the tests but objected to being woken early on race day to provide a blood sample.

The sport's top competitors had pressed for early introduction of the pre-race tests and for defined limits for haemoglobin levels after some abnormally high levels were detected in routine post-race tests, said Bengt Erik Bengtsson of the International Ski Federation (FIS).
Skiers could face similar tests at future World Cup competitions and at the Nagano Winter Olympics next year when cross-country events will be held at Habuka, Bengtsson said.
Fauner finished in 28 minutes 20.2 seconds. Norwegian Erling Jevne placed second and Jari Isometsa of Finland was third.
World Cup leader Bjorn Dahlin finished sixth.

In the women's five-km classic event, Stefania Belmondo of Italy gained ground on World Cup leader Elena Vaelbe of Russia by finishing first in 16:36.6, ahead of Katerina Neumannova of the Czech Republic.
A jet-lagged Vaelbe, who arrived from Moscow only 36 hours before the race, placed third.
The Russians had intended to send six athletes but their contingent was reduced to Vaelbe, a coach and an official after a hold-up in issuing Japanese visas to the team.
Vaelbe received her visa on Wednesday afternoon and left Moscow just hours later.
